body.statement: Let \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\) satisfy \(P_n\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), \(d_n=d\) fixed, \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d\) for every \(k\), and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/M^2\to0\). Then the valid unstudentized conclusions are \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0\) and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0\) in \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability, with \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/M^2\to0\) and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2\to0\). No standardized normal limit, ratio-consistent variance claim, or Wald endpoint-equivalence claim follows from these conditions alone.
body.justification: This separates the valid collapsing-variance statement from the nondegenerate Wald sanity check.
body.gap: Hahn1998 and ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML formulate regular efficiency and Wald inference under nondegeneracy; this proposition records only the unstudentized conclusion supported when the efficient variance vanishes.
body.consumer: Applied users are warned not to report a studentized Gaussian interval merely because the discrete alphabet is fixed.
